head: claude/mi92-board-post-header-drift
title: board-post.yml: header claimed it removes the request file; the code deliberately does not
body:
## Summary

`.github/workflows/board-post.yml`'s Contract block said the runner *"writes the resulting comment URL … **removes the request**, and commits the result back"*.

**It does not remove it, and not removing it is correct.** Nine lines below that sentence sits the comment block explaining why removal was taken out: an earlier version `git rm`'d each request once posted, which made the results commit touch `automation/board-posts/**` — the workflow's own trigger path. The header is stale prose sitting directly above the rationale for the behaviour it misdescribes. **Field beats comment; the header is the half that is wrong.**

## Why this is worth a change rather than a shrug

The stale sentence produces a **false negative on the exact check a session runs to verify its own board post.**

This relay is reached *only* when the MCP's `add_issue_comment` 403s — so the session using it cannot read the board back through the MCP and must verify from the branch. Following the documented contract, it tests *"is the request file gone?"* and reads STILL PRESENT as *"my post failed."*

**Measured while doing exactly that, 2026-09-03:** request file present, result file holding a bare comment URL (`#issuecomment-5523621097`), run exited 0 — a **successful** post that the documented check graded a **failure**.

For a relay whose stated premise is that a failed post must be LOUD — *"a session that believes it claimed the board and did not is invisible to every other session AND to itself"* — this runs the wrong way. The session either **re-posts** (duplicating on #6927) or **reports its own successful claim as failed**.

This is UNPROVENANCED DIAGNOSTIC OUTPUT sub-class A as `CLAUDE.md` defines it: a stated contract naming a condition (`request file removed`) that no code path produces.

## What changed

The header now states what the code does and names the real discriminators — **both already in the code, neither previously in the header**:

| outcome | result file | run |
|---|---|---|
| success | bare comment URL | exit 0 |
| failure | `FAILED:` prefix (line 114) | exit 1 (line 152) |

The old sentence is **recorded rather than silently deleted**, with its cost, so the next session does not re-derive the same wrong check. The lines 80–92 rationale is untouched — it is the reason the behaviour is right.

## Verification

**The one claim worth checking is that the workflow edit is comment-lines-only.** It is verifiable in one command rather than by reading the diff:

```
git diff -U0 .github/workflows/board-post.yml | grep -E '^[+-]' \
  | grep -vE '^(\+\+\+|---)' | grep -vE '^[+-]\s*#'
```

→ returns nothing. The YAML also parses. Triggers, steps and exit codes are untouched.

- [x] `scripts/ci/run_guards.py --base main` — **PASS 48 · FAIL 0 · SKIP 35**
- [x] `pr-landing-guard` — `OK — state=declared_hold`, with `R8 verified — landing machinery in the diff`
- [x] Backlog row filed through `scripts/ops/backlog_append.py` — **12 insertions, 0 deletions**, no reformat churn, so no pre-existing row is re-attributed to this PR

`artifact-validity-guard` failed on the first attempt (the new row had no `resolution_criteria` and no `tier`) and was fixed by a surgical textual edit rather than a JSON rewrite, which would have reformatted the file.

## Architecture impact

- [x] **Not applicable** — comment lines in one workflow header, plus one backlog row.

## ⛔ Landing

**`landing: "hold"` / `hold_reason: "changes_landing_machinery"`.** Tier-1 by every path in the diff, and **the tier is not the objection** — this is held on **R12** alone: a change to the landing machinery must not be merged by that machinery unread, or the change and its own approval are the same act.

I first declared this `landing: "self"`, asserting *"R12 does not apply: board-post.yml is the coordination-board relay, not the landing machinery."* **The guard disagreed and the guard is authoritative about its own scope.** That correction is recorded in the landing file rather than overwritten, so the next session does not re-derive the same wrong boundary.

Filed as `BL-20260903-BOARD-POST-HEADER-CLAIMS-IT-REMOVES-THE-REQUEST-AND-THE-CODE-DELIBERATELY-DOES-NOT`.
